Delivery plan

SequenceQuality gatesChange control

Sequence

The proposed backlog is sequenced using four dimensions:

* Contribution to the product goal.

* Functional and technical dependencies.

* Uncertainty and potential rework.

* Ability to produce a reviewable increment.

The sequence does not imply that discovery and implementation must happen at the same time. High-risk items may require early refinement even when their implementation occurs later.

StageProposed workRationale
Alignment before buildConfirm data authority, selection cardinality, calendar rules, minimum search selection, visual authority and results-page capability (blocking questions)Prevent structural rework and identify production blockers before implementation
Component foundationUS1 — Access the Find a Cruise componentEstablish the common controls, layout and unrestricted initial state
Simple selectionsUS2 — Select a destination; US3 — Select a departure portDeliver independently reviewable selection behavior with limited state complexity
Complex interactionUS4 — Select a departure month rangeAddress the area with the highest interaction and state-transition complexity
Search handoffUS5 — Search using selected filtersConnect the completed criteria with the external Cruises-page capability

This sequence is a delivery recommendation. It does not represent committed sprint allocation or implementation duration.

Quality gates

Acceptance criteria define expected behavior, but they do not by themselves constitute a complete quality or UAT strategy.

The following gates are proposed:

GateDecisionMinimum evidence
Requirements baselineDo Product, UX and Technical stakeholders agree on the intended behavior and scope boundary?Approved backlog, resolved blockers, accepted assumptions
Engineering readinessAre the story’s behavior, data and integration decisions clear enough to begin implementation?Testable acceptance criteria, agreed visual references, identified data owners and dependencies, resolved blocking questions and explicitly accepted remaining assumptions.
Functional QADoes the build conform to the approved specification?Requirement-to-test traceability, passing critical scenarios and documented defects
UATDoes the solution satisfy the intended business and consumer need?Business execution of representative scenarios and a Product Owner decision
Release readinessCan the change be released with understood risk?Accepted defect position, dependency readiness, operational considerations and release approval

Change control

Once a specification baseline is approved, changes should remain possible but controlled.

Each proposed change should be classified as one of the following:

Clarification of an existing requirement.

Confirmation or rejection of a temporary assumption.

New requirement.

UX refinement.

Technical implementation decision outside the functional specification.

The proposed workflow is:

  1. 1. Record the requested change and its source.
  2. 2. Classify the change.
  3. 3. Assess its impact on MVP scope, consumer behavior, state model, data, integration, tests, delivery and documentation.
  4. 4. Identify the accountable decision owner.
  5. 5. Approve, reject or defer the change.
  6. 6. Update the authoritative specification and baseline version before changing implementation behavior.
  7. 7. Update the prototype, traceability and tests where applicable.
  8. 8. Revalidate all affected scenarios.
  9. 9. Communicate the resulting baseline and any delivery impact.

Example

The current proposal assumes that when the second selected month is earlier than the provisional start month, the earlier month becomes the new start and no end month remains selected.

If the Product Owner decides instead that the two selected months should be reordered automatically, this would change:

* The functional specification.

* The date-selection state model.

* The corresponding acceptance criteria.

* Prototype behavior.

* Automated and browser test scenarios.

* UAT coverage.

The decision should therefore follow the change-control workflow instead of entering implementation as an undocumented user-interface adjustment.
